about: The card-triage need vocabulary beyond top-commanders-gaps.json's features: every key a blocked record in data/sweep-*/ uses resolves through `aliases` to one of those features or to an entry in `features` here (a narrower need, filed under its `family`). `example` is the first record that named it. A need that lands goes into top-commanders-gaps.json's `built` array, whichever file defines it. Tooling: npm run cards:needs -w engine (scripts/needs-vocabulary.mjs).

bug:additional-cost-option-affordability.example: Eaten Alive: Its "pay {3}{B}" additional-cost option is offered even when the mana can't be paid, and taking it throws (fuzzer seeds 4, 27, 31).

bug:attackers-through-end-of-combat.example: Desert: engine clears attacking status as the end of combat step begins (rule 511.3 says as it ends), so 'target attacking creature' during that step has no legal target

bug:cda-cards-exiled-with.example: Unlicensed Hearse: No 'up to two targets from a single graveyard' relation, nor a P/T CDA counting cards exiled with it.

bug:cda-counter-total.example: Toph, the Blind Bandit: CDA power = +1/+1 counters on lands you control: no counter-sum CountSpec for setBasePtFromCount

bug:cda-devotion.example: Daxos, Blessed by the Sun: Toughness equal to devotion to white: a CDA count can't read devotion.

bug:cda-sum-of-counts.example: Abomination of Llanowar: CDA is Elves you control plus Elf cards in your graveyard — setBasePtFromCount takes a single CountSpec, no sum.

bug:commander-mv-battlefield-or-command-.example: Majestic Genesis: greatestCommanderManaValue counts commanders in every zone; card counts only battlefield and command zone

bug:creature-subtype-needs-creature-type.example: Archangel Elspeth: add-types keeps a non-copiable Angel subtype on a permanent that stops being a creature; the ruling says it stops being an Angel.

bug:defending-player-after-removal.example: Armix, Filigree Thrasher: Reflexive target 'creature defending player controls' reads live attacking; rule 508.5 keeps the defending player if Armix left combat.

bug:delayed-sacrifice-by-you.example: Come Back Wrong: sacrifice-target makes the permanent's current controller sacrifice it; the card has you sacrifice it, so it does nothing if someone else has taken control

bug:distinct-targets-across-slots.example: Ghostly Flicker: 'Two target …' needs two different objects, but separate target slots aren't checked against each other. The reviewer had a cast with the same permanent in both slots accepted.

bug:disturb-exile-replacement-as-ability.example: Lunarch Veteran: Luminous Phantom's "exile it instead" is done by the disturb cast path, not as its own ability, so a copy doesn't exile and Humility doesn't stop it (Hook-Haunt Drifter shares it).

bug:each-player-reanimate-simultaneous.example: Exhume: each player's chosen card must enter simultaneously; for-each-player look-and-choose moves them one at a time

bug:extort-life-lost.example: Crypt Ghast: The extort helper gains one life per opponent rather than the life actually lost (ruling: with Platinum Emperion you gain nothing). The Swamp mana trigger is expressible.

bug:found-card-wherever-it-went.example: Oriq Loremage: "If it's an instant or sorcery card" reads only a card that reached the graveyard; under Rest in Peace the found card is exiled and should still count.

bug:granted-trigger-identity.example: Dionus, Elvish Archdruid: once-each-turn is tracked per ability index of the Elf, so a new Dionus's grant (a different ability per the ruling) or two Dionuses' grants can't be told apart

bug:mana-trigger-color-choice.example: Fertile Ground: 'Adds an additional one mana of any color' on a land tapped by hand: a tapped-for-mana extra of any colour is made white there, with no choice.

bug:milled-cards-in-any-public-zone.example: Bramble Familiar: Fetch Quest looks for the milled cards only in the graveyard; with Rest in Peace they're in exile and it should still find them (rule 701.17c).

bug:mixed-simultaneous-entry.example: Sword of Hearth and Home: The exiled creature and the found basic land enter together; a flicker and a search are two entries.

bug:oring-one-shot-return.example: Cast Out: its ruling: the card returns immediately as Cast Out leaves, nothing in between; the engine's O-Ring return is a leaves-battlefield trigger on the stack

bug:play-mdfc-land-face-from-graveyard.example: Ancient Greenwarden: 'You may play lands from your graveyard' should let you play an MDFC's land back face (ruling). playFromGraveyard matches the card's front face, so the permission misses it. The trigger-doubling half is fine.

bug:return-from-graveyard-reads-x.example: Ascend from Avernus: return-from-graveyard's filter isn't given the spell's X

bug:return-source-card-from-graveyard.example: Journey to Eternity: 'then return this card transformed' needs the Aura's new graveyard object; 'source' is lost after its zone change

bug:return-transformed-non-dfc-stays-exi.example: The Restoration of Eiganjo: ruling: a non-DFC told to return transformed stays in exile; flicker transformed returns it as usual; no transforming-Saga precedent

bug:return-without-abilities-as-it-enter.example: Xu-Ifit, Osteoharmonist: ruling: loses ETB/as-enters abilities before they apply; engine would add the type/ability loss after it enters

bug:reveal-from-hand-reads-changeling.example: Murmuring Bosk: Reveal a Treefolk card from hand: revealableFromHand reads printed subtypes, so a changeling card isn't offered (rule 702.73a).

bug:reveal-or-control-condition.example: Temple of the Dragon Queen: Enters tapped unless you revealed a Dragon card or control a Dragon: the reveal and the board condition each force it tapped (an AND), not either one sparing it.

bug:saga-exile-return-transformed.example: Welcome to . . .: Per-opponent artifact animation 'for as long as you control this Saga' plus exile-and-return transformed into Jurassic Park.

bug:self-or-another-trigger.example: Beregond of the Guard: "This or another X" as one trigger misses its own entry when it isn't an X (a copy, Conspiracy); needs the self + otherOnly split.

bug:spell-copy-keeps-sacrificed.example: Tend the Pests: Ruling: copies use the original's sacrificed creature's power, but copySpellFrom doesn't carry lastKnownRefs.sacrificed, so a copy would make 0 Pests

bug:spell-target-filter-reads-x.example: Profane Command: 'Up to X target creatures gain fear' (a target count of X in a castModal mode) and 'creature card with mana value X or less' in a spell's target filter (AUTHORING §6: a spell's target filter can't read X).

bug:split-half-colors.example: Life: Life // Death's halves have different colours (rule 709.3); no pool split card has differing halves yet, and card:verify compares halves to the whole card's colours.

bug:stacking-draw-replacements.example: Phial of Galadriel: ruling: two Phials draw three; engine takes the max of 'draw N instead' replacements (drawCountFor) rather than applying each

bug:target-filter-x-activated.example: Lazotep Quarry: A target with mana value X on an activated ability, untested; left for a check.

bug:target-permanent-of-targeting-player.example: Scalelord Reckoner: 'that player' (the opponent who targeted the Dragon) as a permanent target's controller is unconfirmed for becomes-target triggers

bug:this-cycled-trigger.example: Dismantling Wave: 'For each opponent, … up to one target … that player controls': target options are filtered by a pure function with no state (slotOptions), so one-per-opponent needs plumbing through the offer, validation, client and bot

bug:token-copy-as-enters-choices.example: Ardyn, the Usurper: ruling says the token copy's 'as enters' abilities work; a token copy isn't asked them (§15)

bug:trigger-relative-target-filter.example: Gale, Waterdeep Prodigy: Target 'card of the other type' depends on the triggering spell's type; only expressible by splitting the one ability into two triggers.

bug:turn-history-descended-as-it-arrived.example: Raphael, Fiendish Savior: descended filter reads the card as it is now, not as it was put into the graveyard

condition:adamant-colorless.example: Desecrate Reality: no even/odd mana value filter; adamant on colorless mana unverified

condition:any-graveyard-size-condition.example: Visions of Beyond: conditions only count your own graveyard, not 'a graveyard has twenty or more cards'

condition:attached-host-condition.example: Champion's Helm: "As long as equipped creature is legendary, it has hexproof": no static condition asks about the permanent an Equipment is attached to.

condition:attacking-alone-condition.example: Security Bypass: 'as long as enchanted creature is attacking alone, it can't be blocked' has no StaticCondition

condition:attacking-an-opponent-filter.example: Oviya, Automech Artisan: 'attacking one of your opponents' (not a planeswalker) has no filter; put creature/Vehicle from hand with conditional artifact counters also unproven

condition:cant-be-blocked-except-by-flyi.example: Signal Pest: CardFilter has only one notKeyword; can't say 'neither flying nor reach'

condition:card-left-graveyard-condition.example: Essence Anchor: 'Activate only if a card left your graveyard this turn' — the used-graveyard-this-turn condition asks something else (a spell cast or ability activated from a graveyard).

condition:cards-currently-exiled-with-so.example: Evercoat Ursine: intervening-if 'if there are cards exiled with it' means still in exile; the exiled-with-source condition counts cards ever exiled, so the trigger would still fire after both were played

condition:cast-timing-condition.example: Return to Dust: 'If you cast this spell during your main phase' gates the second target on how it was cast.

condition:compare-each-other-player.example: Battle Angels of Tyr: Myriad plus checks against each other player's hand and lands.

condition:compare-to-chosen-value.example: Talion, the Kindly Lord: 'Choose a number between 1 and 10' as it enters, then matching a spell's mana value, power or toughness to it, has no filter comparison against a chosen value, and the choice would only fire when it's cast.

condition:condition-cards-in-all-graveya.example: Avatar of Woe: cards-in-graveyard condition reads only your own graveyard, not all graveyards

condition:condition-count-all-permanents.example: Hour of Revelation: no condition for "ten or more nonland permanents on the battlefield" across all players

condition:condition-lands-same-name.example: Endless Atlas: no condition for 'three or more lands with the same name'

condition:condition-not-casters-turn.example: Scytheclaw Raptor: no intervening-if for 'not the caster's turn' (trigger-object condition reads false at trigger time)

condition:control-distinct-names-count.example: Maze's End: no condition for 'ten or more Gates with different names'

condition:counter-parity-condition.example: Sab-Sunen, Luxa Embodied: can't attack/block unless an even number of counters, and draw if odd: no parity condition over counters

condition:coven.example: Leinore, Autumn Sovereign: no condition for three creatures with different powers (AUTHORING §15)

condition:distinct-names-condition.example: Liliana's Contract: 'four or more Demons with different names' intervening-if: only distinctTokenNames (tokens) exists

condition:dynamic-compare-in-static-filt.example: Champion of Lambholt: 'Creatures with power less than this creature's power can't block creatures you control' — a static's cantBeBlockedBy filter can't compare against the source's live power (an { amount } operand fails closed there).

condition:dynamic-operand-in-intervening.example: Padeem, Consul of Innovation: "If you control the artifact with the greatest mana value" compares with a live maximum, which a trigger's intervening-if can't read.

condition:entered-from-graveyard.example: Kotis, Sibsig Champion: Casting a creature from your graveyard by exiling three other cards (escape would wrongly mark it escaped), and 'entered from a graveyard or was cast from a graveyard'.

condition:equipment-attached-count-condi.example: Brass Knuckles: cast-trigger self copy of a permanent spell and 'two or more Equipment attached' condition

condition:exiled-with-source-count.example: Colfenor's Urn: 'If three or more cards have been exiled with this artifact', then return those cards.

condition:filter-attacking-your-opponent.example: Martial Impetus: no filter for 'creature attacking one of your opponents'

condition:filter-controlled-by-trigger-p.example: Hellkite Tyrant: "You win the game", and "gain control of all artifacts that player controls" — no filter clause names the damaged player.

condition:filter-has-tap-activated-abili.example: Magewright's Stone: no CardFilter clause for 'has an activated ability with {T} in its cost'

condition:filter-same-name-as-source.example: Callidus Assassin: no target filter for 'creature with the same name as this creature'

condition:filter-shares-creature-type-wi.example: Folk Hero: sharesCreatureTypeWith only reads the trigger object, not the granted ability's holder

condition:filter-total-power-toughness.example: Cut Down: no filter for total power plus toughness

condition:filter-x-in-mana-cost.example: Frontline Medic: no battalion trigger; no 'spell with {X} in its mana cost' filter

condition:greatest-power-condition.example: Summon: Fenrir: Chapter II and III.

condition:hand-filter-land-count.example: Anticausal Vestige: A permanent card with mana value up to your land count from hand (BACKLOG).

condition:if-kicked-enters-with-counters.example: Gnarlid Colony: no enters-with-counters conditional on (single) kicker

condition:intervening-if-amounts.example: Liberator, Urza's Battlethopter: 'If the amount of mana spent to cast that spell is greater than Liberator's power' is an intervening-if rechecked on resolution; a condition's `{ amount }` operand fails closed.

condition:intervening-if-not-trigger-pla.example: Price of Glory: no trigger condition for 'if it's not that player's turn' on another player's mana tap

condition:life-above-starting.example: Righteous Valkyrie: 'At least 7 life more than your starting life total'.

condition:linked-exile-currently-exiled.example: Ugin's Labyrinth: needs 'if a card is (currently) exiled with this' mana amount and 'return the exiled card to hand'; exiled-with-source counts ever-exiled

condition:named-artifact-condition.example: Wedding Ring: An opponent gets a copy; triggers on opponents controlling an artifact named Wedding Ring.

condition:no-abilities-filter.example: Ruxa, Patient Professor: no 'creature with no abilities' filter nor optional assign-as-though-unblocked static

condition:no-other-creature-greater-powe.example: Getaway Glamer: 'if no other creature has greater power' condition not expressed

condition:return-cards-put-in-graveyard-.example: Faith's Reward: no filter for cards put into graveyard from the battlefield this turn

condition:same-name-as-target.example: Maelstrom Pulse: No filter for 'all other permanents with the same name as that permanent'.

condition:shares-creature-type-with-equi.example: Stoneforge Masterwork: sharesCreatureTypeWith only reads a trigger object; no count of creatures sharing a type with the equipped creature.

condition:some-opponent-controls-none.example: Hagra Mauling // Hagra Broodpit: 'Costs {1} less if an opponent controls no basic lands' — one opponent with none.

condition:that-player-controls-more.example: Archaeomancer's Map: "If that player controls more lands than you": opponent-controls-more asks about any opponent, not the one whose land entered.

condition:trigger-condition-casters-turn.example: March of the World Ooze: "if it's not their turn" (the casting opponent's) has no condition; not-your-turn is wrong in multiplayer

condition:turn-count-condition.example: Starting Town: "Unless it's your first, second, or third turn of the game": no per-player count of turns taken.

condition:void-condition.example: Elegy Acolyte: Void (a nonland permanent left the battlefield or a spell was warped this turn) has no StaticCondition.

condition:werewolf-transform-spells-last.example: Duskwatch Recruiter: No condition for spells cast last turn (werewolf transform triggers).

condition:you-have-most-life-trigger-con.example: Preacher of the Schism: second trigger 'attacks while you have the most life or tied' has no condition (first is defenderLife most)

cost:additional-cost-discard-filter.example: Magmatic Insight: additionalCost.discard has no card filter (discard a land card)

cost:additional-cost-reveal.example: Thunderherd Migration: no "reveal a Dinosaur card from your hand" additional-cost option

cost:alt-cost-discard-cards.example: Foil: alternative cost 'discard an Island card and another card' isn't expressible

cost:alt-cost-exile-from-hand.example: Commandeer: Gaining control of a spell, and exiling two blue cards as its cost.

cost:alt-cost-opponent-gains-life.example: Invigorate: no alternative cost of having an opponent gain life

cost:alt-cost-pay-life-equal-mana-value.example: Demon of Fate's Design: once-per-turn alternative cost of life equal to mana value, and +X/+0 from the sacrificed enchantment's MV, not expressible together

cost:alt-cost-return-lands.example: Gush: No alternative cost of returning two Islands to hand.

cost:alt-cost-sacrifice.example: Flare of Cultivation: 'Sacrifice a nontoken green creature rather than pay this spell's mana cost', and a two-way search split.

cost:alternative-cost-for-all-spells.example: Leyline of Mutation: leyline opening-hand rule plus WUBRG alt cost for every spell

cost:alternative-cost-for-spells-limits.example: Darksteel Monolith: alternativeCostForSpells has no once-each-turn limit and no cast-from-hand restriction.

cost:alternative-cost-pay-life.example: Snuff Out: 'you may pay 4 life rather than pay this spell's mana cost' if you control a Swamp

cost:attack-tax.example: Propaganda: "Creatures can't attack you unless their controller pays {2} for each creature attacking you" — no attack-cost mechanism.

cost:attack-tax-per-counters.example: Nils, Discipline Enforcer: attackTax is a fixed generic amount, not X = counters on the attacking creature, and not covering your planeswalkers

cost:chosen-type-menu-spend-restriction.example: Eclipsed Realms: spendOnly.chosenType reads chooseCreatureTypeOnEnter (any type); no way to limit the menu to the eight listed types

cost:chosen-type-sacrifice-cost.example: Etchings of the Chosen: sacrifice-cost filters are matched with no source, so ofChosenType matches nothing

cost:conditional-alternative-cost.example: Blasphemous Edict: 'You may pay {B} rather than pay this spell's mana cost if there are thirteen or more creatures' — alternativeCost has no condition and always taps creatures; freeCastIf is only free.

cost:cost-increase-not-your-turn.example: Defense Grid: Spells cost more except during their controller's turn.

cost:cost-mod-by-cast-zone.example: Gravebreaker Lamia: costModification can't select spells by the zone they're cast from (graveyard)

cost:cost-modification-by-spell-targets.example: Kasmina, Enigmatic Mentor: can't tax opponents' spells by what they target

cost:cost-move-linked-exiled-card.example: Shelob, Dread Weaver: cost 'put a creature card exiled with Shelob into its owner's graveyard' and X-matched linked-exile target

cost:cost-reduction-creatures-died-this-.example: Blood for the Blood God!: CostReductionAmount has no 'creatures that died this turn' count.

cost:cost-reduction-for-targeting-enchan.example: Strong Back: equip/Aura cost reductions only when targeting the enchanted creature aren't expressible

cost:cost-reduction-greatest-opponent-co.example: Cavern-Hoard Dragon: Costs {X} less where X is the greatest number of artifacts an opponent controls; its combat-damage Treasures count the damaged player's artifacts.

cost:cost-reduction-if-targets.example: Price of Fame: self cost reduction conditioned on the chosen target

cost:cost-reduction-permanents-sacrifice.example: The Balrog, Durin's Bane: no 'permanents sacrificed this turn' cost-reduction count

cost:counter-cost.example: Wall of Roots: Putting a -0/-1 counter on itself as a cost.

cost:creatures-attacked-this-turn-count.example: Rowdy Research: '{1} less for each creature that attacked this turn': no cost-reduction amount counts attackers this turn, including ones no longer on the battlefield (the `attacked` turn stat is only 0/1).

cost:cycling-alt-cost.example: Edge of Autumn: Cycling with a sacrifice-a-land cost has no shape

cost:depletion-counter-lands.example: Hickory Woodlot: enters with depletion counters, sacrifice if none left; no pool precedent

cost:discard-x-cost.example: Gix, Yawgmoth Praetor: 'Discard X cards' as a cost, and a may-pay-life draw per creature.

cost:dynamic-life-cost.example: War Room: "Pay life equal to the number of colors in your commanders' color identity": an activation cost's payLife is a fixed number, and nothing reads the commanders' colour identity.

cost:equip-ability-cost-reduction.example: Bladehold War-Whip: abilityCostModification can't single out equip abilities of other Equipment.

cost:equip-alternative-costs.example: Gavel of the Righteous: +1/+1 per counter of any kind (grantPtPerCount.countersOnSource takes one kind) and 'Equip—Pay {3} or remove a counter'

cost:equip-cost-per-color.example: Dragonfire Blade: Hexproof from monocolored; equip cost by the target's colors.

cost:exile-creature-cost.example: Food Chain: Exiling a creature as a cost, with mana from its mana value.

cost:exile-many-cost-linked-return.example: Mechtitan Core: exile-five-permanents cost, linked return on token leaving, and all-colors token not expressible

cost:exile-x-cards-cost.example: Necropolis Fiend: 'Exile X cards from your graveyard' as a cost. (Delve is built, 2026-10-02.)

cost:flashback-cost-reduction.example: Visions of Glory: No reduction applying only to the flashback cast by commander mana value (battlefield or command zone).

cost:flashback-exile-x-cost.example: Summons of Saruman: Flashback cost 'Exile X cards from your graveyard' and casting a free spell from among the milled cards aren't expressible.

cost:free-cast-from-hand-static.example: Omniscience: 'You may cast spells from your hand without paying their mana costs': alternativeCostForSpells can't be limited to the hand, and a card with an alternative cost of its own would be offered only that one.

cost:free-cast-once-each-turn.example: As Foretold: 'Once each turn, you may pay {0} rather than pay the mana cost' for spells up to its time counters.

cost:kicker-nonmana-cost.example: Primal Growth: kicker cost is a sacrifice; kicker.cost is mana only

cost:loyalty-x.example: Tezzeret the Seeker: A −X loyalty ability.

cost:mana-restriction-cast-from-graveyar.example: Lord of the Forsaken: Mana spendable only to cast a spell from your graveyard: a mana restriction can't ask the spell's zone.

cost:mana-spend-only-x-costs.example: Nexos: no ManaRestriction for 'only on costs that contain {X}'

cost:mill-cost.example: Millikin: '{T}, Mill a card: Add {C}' — milling as a cost.

cost:minus-zero-minus-one-counters.example: Wall of Roots: Putting a -0/-1 counter on itself as a cost.

cost:multiple-alternative-costs.example: Dracogenesis: An alternative cost for Dragon spells; with Jodah, Archmage Eternal out too, the engine offers only the first alternative cost it finds rather than the player's choice.

cost:optional-life-additional-cost-for-s.example: Defiler of Dreams: optional pay-2-life additional cost reducing {U} on other spells not expressible

cost:pay-any-amount-of-energy.example: Aether Refinery: No replacement on getting {E}, and no 'pay one or more {E}' with X = amount paid.

cost:pay-variable-energy.example: Jolted Awake: pay energy equal to a target card's mana value, if you do return it: no precedent

cost:pay-x-energy.example: Sphinx of the Revelation: payEnergy is a fixed number; 'Pay X {E}: Draw X cards' needs a variable energy cost

cost:put-counter-cost.example: Devoted Druid: "Put a -1/-1 counter on this creature" as a cost.

cost:remove-any-counter-cost.example: Glen Elendra Guardian: 'Remove a counter' of any kind; removeCounter cost takes one fixed kind

cost:remove-x-counters-cost.example: Hourglass of the Lost: Activated cost removes a fixed count; 'Remove X time counters' with X read by the effect isn't expressible.

cost:return-lands-cost.example: Multani, Yavimaya's Avatar: 'Return two lands you control to their owner's hand' as a cost.

cost:return-self-to-hand-cost.example: Chthonian Nightmare: Pay X {E} and return this enchantment to its owner's hand as costs.

cost:reveal-any-number-from-hand.example: Metalworker: mana scaled by revealing any number of artifact cards from hand

cost:reveal-card-as-additional-cost.example: Calamity of the Titans: Reveal a colorless creature card as an additional cost, then exile by MV below the revealed card's

cost:sacrifice-cost-mv-x-plus-one.example: Sidisi, Regent of the Mire: sacrifice a creature with MV X, return card with MV X+1

cost:spend-colorless-as-any-color.example: Abstruse Appropriation: no 'spend colorless mana as though any color' cast permission

cost:spend-only-cast-from-exile.example: Interdimensional Web Watch: ManaRestriction has no 'only to cast spells from exile' clause

cost:tap-cost-transform-trigger.example: Thousand Moons Smithy // Barracks of the Thousand: Tapping five permanents as an optional trigger cost to transform, and mana-provenance tokens.

cost:tap-x-untapped-cost.example: Secluded Starforge: tapOthers count is a fixed number, not X

cost:targeted-by-spells-mana-tax.example: Jubilant Skybonder: Grants fliers 'spells your opponents cast that target this creature cost {2} more': targetedBySpellsCost is payLife only and only on its own permanent.

cost:transform-land-cost-reduction-per-t.example: Balamb Garden, SeeD Academy: activated transform with per-Town cost reduction; back face too

cost:unattach-cost.example: Sunforger: Unattach as a cost, and cast a searched card free.

cost:untap-cost.example: Halo Fountain: Untapping creatures as a cost, and 'you win the game'.

cost:untap-symbol-cost.example: Umbral Mantle: A granted '{3}, {Q}' ability; there's no untap-symbol cost.

decision:any-number-max.example: Baldin, Century Herdmaster: 'Up to one hundred target creatures': an any-number target group has no maximum.

decision:any-number-targets-in-mode.example: Klauth's Will: Its second mode deals damage divided among any number of targets; the engine allows an any-number target group only as the last slot of a non-modal list (any-number-targets.test.ts).

decision:attacker-chooses-blocks.example: Odric, Master Tactician: no way for the attacking player to declare the defenders' blocks

decision:cast-one-per-card-type-from-exi.example: Aminatou's Augury: for each nonland card type, one free cast of that type from the exiled cards

decision:cast-up-to-n-free.example: Plargg and Nassari: Each player exiles until a nonland card, an opponent picks one, and you may cast up to two of the others free.

decision:choose-any-number-different-nam.example: Eerie Ultimatum: Any number of permanent cards with different names from your graveyard, chosen as it resolves.

decision:choose-card-name.example: Phyrexian Revoker: no 'choose a card name' as it enters / named-source ability lock

decision:choose-card-per-graveyard.example: Breach the Multiverse: "For each player, choose a creature or planeswalker card in that player's graveyard", all put onto the battlefield under your control together.

decision:choose-card-type-protection.example: Serra's Emissary: no chosen card type as-enters, no player protection from a card type

decision:choose-color-on-resolution.example: Oona, Queen of the Fae: choose a colour on resolution and count exiled cards of that colour

decision:choose-counter-kind.example: Ichormoon Gauntlet: can't grant loyalty abilities to planeswalkers or 'choose a counter on target permanent'

decision:choose-creature-type-on-resolut.example: Kindred Summons: Choose a creature type, then reveal until X creature cards of it.

decision:choose-from-any-graveyard.example: Soul of Windgrace: "Put a land card from a graveyard onto the battlefield tapped under your control" is untargeted and reaches every graveyard; return-from-graveyard and look-and-choose only reach your own.

decision:choose-from-batch.example: Colossal Grave-Reaver: 'Put one of them onto the battlefield' from the creature cards milled together.

decision:choose-from-hand-and-graveyard.example: Worldsoul's Rage: "Put up to X land cards from your hand and/or graveyard onto the battlefield tapped" is one choice across two zones and one simultaneous entry; look-and-choose reads one zone.
