effect:choose-per-opponent-then-destroy.example: Ultimate Magic: Meteor: Ultimate Magic: Meteor: "for each opponent, choose an artifact or land that player controls. Destroy the chosen permanents" — one untargeted pick from each opponent's permanents, then all destroyed together.

effect:grant-harmonize.example: A card in your graveyard gains harmonize until end of turn, its harmonize cost equal to its mana cost — grant-flashback's shape for harmonize (Songcrafter Mage).

condition:source-hasnt-dealt-damage.example: True while this permanent hasn't dealt any damage, combat or noncombat, since it entered the battlefield (Karakyk Guardian); condition:source-hasnt-dealt-combat-damage is the combat-only form.

effect:exile-chosen-from-revealed-hand.example: Target opponent reveals their hand; you choose a card matching a filter from it and exile it (discard-chosen's choice, moving the card to exile instead of the graveyard) - Aggressive Negotiations.

cost:cost-increase-if-targets.example: "This spell costs {N} more to cast if it targets [filter]" - the increase counterpart of targetCostReduction, applied before reductions (rule 601.2f) and only when a chosen target matches - Dragon's Prey.

condition:counter-kinds-among-permanents.example: A StaticCondition for N or more different kinds of counters among the permanents you control matching a filter (each kind counted once, wherever it sits) — Hundred-Battle Veteran.

replacement:as-enters-exile-from-graveya.example: An 'as this enters, exile up to X [filter] cards from your graveyard' choice made before the permanent moves, linked to it, with 'enters with N counters for each card exiled this way' (Mimeoplasm, Revered One).

trigger:crews-or-saddles.example: A trigger when this creature crews a Vehicle or saddles a Mount (rule 702.122b / 702.171), its trigger object the crewed or saddled permanent, optionally only during your main phase (Canyon Vaulter).

trigger:activates-exhaust.example: The activates-ability trigger narrowed to an exhaust ability ('whenever you activate an exhaust ability' — Adrenaline Jockey), as ninjutsu and loyalty already narrow it. Haunted Screen's plain "Activate only once" uses the same `exhaust: true` flag (once per object), so the trigger must check the Exhaust keyword, not that flag.

static:pt-per-life-total.example: A layer-7 P/T modification scaled by the controller's life total ('gets -X/-X, where X is your life total' — The Last Ride); grantPtPerCount has no lifeTotal source.

static:exhaust-reactivation.example: Elvish Refueler: during your turn, if you haven't activated an exhaust ability this turn, exhaust abilities may be activated as though they hadn't been (a per-turn exhaust-activation record and a waiver of the once-only check).

cost:ability-cost-reduction-exhaust.example: abilityCostModification narrowed to exhaust abilities: 'Exhaust abilities of other permanents you control cost {2} less to activate' (Boom Scholar), able to take the mana component to {0}.

effect:reduce-player-speed.example: Lower another player's speed by N with a floor of 1, gated on that player's speed being greater than each other player's (Spikeshell Harrier).

cost:alternative-cost-for-spells-energy.example: alternativeCostForSpells paid in energy rather than mana: 'You may pay eight {E} rather than pay the mana cost for permanent spells you cast' (Nissa, Worldsoul Speaker).

effect:tapped-for-mana-land-deals-damage.example: A triggered mana ability (rule 605.1b) that, besides adding mana, has the tapped land deal damage to the player who tapped it ('then that land deals 1 damage to that player' — Barbflare Gremlin); tappedForManaExtras only adds mana.

condition:milled-share-all-card-types.example: A this-way condition true when two of the cards milled this way have exactly the same combination of card types (supertypes and subtypes ignored — Demonic Covenant's 'if two cards that share all their card types were milled this way').

condition:power-parity.example: Odd/even parity of a power: a source condition ("as long as ~'s power is even" — Kianne, Corrupted Memory) and a CardFilter/NumCompare clause ("each creature with power of the chosen quality" — Zimone's Hypothesis).

decision:choose-any-number-different-pow.example: A look-and-choose set rule that the chosen cards all have different powers (Rip, Spawn Hunter's "any number of creature and/or Vehicle cards with different powers").

trigger:manifests-dread.example: "Whenever you manifest dread" (fires even when the manifest dread couldn't be completed), with the card that manifest dread put into the graveyard readable by its effect (Paranormal Analyst).

effect:amount-unlocked-doors.example: An EffectAmount counting unlocked doors among Rooms you control (Misty Salon's X/X Spirit).

effect:beheld-object-amount.example: A spell's effect reading the object beheld for its additional cost: its power on resolution, or last-known if it left the battlefield (Monstrous Emergence).

condition:prime-count.example: A condition that you control a prime number of permanents matching a filter (Zimone, All-Questioning's 'you control a prime number of lands').

condition:not-attached-to-source.example: A CardFilter clause excluding (or matching) the permanent the filtering source is attached to — Sporogenic Infection's 'sacrifices a creature other than enchanted creature'.

stat:turned-face-up-this-turn.example: Turn tallies of permanents a player turned face up and of permanents that entered face down under them (judged as they entered) — Oblivious Bookworm's 'unless a permanent entered the battlefield face down under your control this turn or you turned a permanent face up this turn'.

zone:graveyard-cast-rider-own-permission.example: Record which grant a graveyard cast used, so a card's own 'you may cast this card from your graveyard … If you do, it enters with a +1/+1 counter' rider (Undead Sprinter) applies only under its own permission, not Gisa and Geralf's or Kotis's.

condition:card-types-in-graveyard-thresh.example: A condition 'N or more card types among cards in your graveyard' for N other than delirium's four (Omnivorous Flytrap's six).

effect:targets-same-controller.example: A target slot relation requiring a later slot's object to have the same controller as an earlier slot's (Trial of Agony's "two target creatures controlled by the same opponent"), the mirror of differentController, rechecked as the spell resolves.

cost:spend-only-unlock-door.example: A spend restriction admitting the cost of unlocking a Room's door (the unlock-door special action, rule 709.5e) — Creeping Peeper's "Spend this mana only to cast an enchantment spell, unlock a door, or turn a permanent face up".

cost:additional-cost-tap-permanents.example: A spell's additional cost of tapping N untapped permanents you control matching a filter ('tap two untapped creatures and/or lands you control' — Fear of Exposure), chosen as the cost is paid; tapOthers exists only on activated abilities and alternativeCost.tapCreatures only as an alternative cost.

stat:trigger-only-once-per-object.example: 'This ability triggers only once' (Acrobatic Cheerleader): a triggered ability that triggers at most once for as long as its object exists — not reset each turn, and spent even if the trigger is countered; a new object (it left and came back) may trigger again.

condition:unlocked-door-count.example: A StaticCondition counting unlocked doors among Rooms you control — Rampaging Soulrager's 'two or more unlocked doors among Rooms you control' (a fully unlocked Room counts two).

condition:card-types-among-exiled-with-s.example: A static condition on the number of card types among the cards currently exiled with the source (linked exile, rule 607.2a) — Keen-Eyed Curator's "as long as there are four or more card types among cards exiled with this creature".

condition:equipped-by-filter.example: A CardFilter clause for having an attached Equipment that matches a filter — "a creature you control with a legendary Equipment attached to it" (Kassandra, Eagle Bearer).

condition:target-player-turn-stat.example: A conditional on a turn stat of the player in a target slot — Thought-Stalker Warlock's 'if they [target opponent] lost life this turn'; turn-stat's who is only you / opponent / any-player.

cost:ability-tap-creatures-for-mana.example: An activated ability whose generic mana may each be paid by tapping an untapped creature you control instead (Heirloom Epic) — waterbend's per-generic tapping restricted to creatures, summoning-sick ones included.

cost:exile-from-graveyard-total-mana-val.example: An activation cost of exiling any number of cards from your graveyard matching a filter whose total mana value is N or greater (The Capitoline Triad's "with total mana value 30 or greater"): a chosen set gated on a sum, not a count.

cost:forage.example: Forage as a cost (rule 701.61a): an activated ability's "Forage:" cost (mana abilities included) and a spell's "as an additional cost, forage or pay …" option — choose exile three graveyard cards or sacrifice a Food while paying, offered only when one is possible, and count as foraging for "whenever you forage".

cost:freerunning-non-mana.example: A freerunning cost that isn't mana — Escape Detection's 'Freerunning—Return a blue creature you control to its owner's hand' (rule 702.173a).

effect:act-on-discarded-card.example: An effect target naming the card a resolution discarded — "if the discarded card was an artifact card, exile it from your graveyard; if you do, create a token copy of it" (Leonardo da Vinci).

effect:choose-add-or-remove-counter.example: Sigurd, Jarl of Ravensthorpe's boast: 'put a lore counter on target Saga you control or remove one from it', the choice made on resolution.

effect:cloak-exiled-pile.example: Cloak a shuffled face-down pile of exiled cards — a creature you own plus library cards — entering tapped (Become Anonymous); manifest's cloak reaches only a library's top card.

effect:delayed-trigger-on-play-this-way.example: Until end of turn, a trigger whenever you play a land or cast a spell using this effect's permission ("its owner draws a card" — Apple of Eden, Isu Relic).

effect:enters-with-counters-if-type.example: put-onto-battlefield withCounters gated on a type judged as the permanent enters (rule 614.12) — "it enters with two additional +1/+1 counters on it if it's a creature" (What Must Be Done).

effect:search-hand-graveyard-library.example: search-library zones including the hand — "search your graveyard, hand, and library for a card named X, put it onto the battlefield, then shuffle" (Kassandra, Eagle Bearer).

effect:search-split-count.example: search-library's split with a count for `destination` before `restDestination` takes the rest — 'put two of them onto the battlefield tapped and the other into your hand' (Viewpoint Synchronization), the first N finds (all when N or fewer) going to `destination`.

effect:search-zones-chosen-by-target-pla.example: A 'target player searches their library and/or graveyard … if they search their library this way, they shuffle' where the searching player, not the effect's controller, chooses which zones (Auditore Ambush); the resolution modal is always answered by the controller.

effect:temporary-opponent-spell-tax.example: A player-effect raising the cost of opponents' spells for a duration — "until your next turn, spells your opponents cast cost {1} more to cast" (Tax Collector).

filter:has-freerunning.example: A CardFilter clause for a card or spell that has freerunning (a non-null `freerunning` field, from any zone) — 'a spell that has freerunning' (Brotherhood Headquarters' spend restriction), 'card with freerunning' (Jacob Frye's target).

keyword:detain.example: Detain (rule 701.35): until your next turn, the permanent can't attack or block and its activated abilities (mana abilities included) can't be activated (Tax Collector, the RTR detain cards).

keyword:valiant.example: Valiant (Bloomburrow): 'whenever this creature becomes the target of a spell or ability you control for the first time each turn' — a becomes-target trigger limited to its controller's spells and abilities (the mirror of byOpponentOnly) and firing only the first time each turn that permanent is so targeted, counting targets changed or copies' targets (the rulings).

static:lose-keyword.example: A static that makes the affected permanents lose a keyword in layer 6, in timestamp order with grants — 'Equipped creature gets +3/+3 and loses flying' (Starforged Sword).

trigger:counters-put-each-counter.example: Sigurd, Jarl of Ravensthorpe: 'whenever you put a lore counter on a Saga' triggers once per counter put (rule 603.2c), not once per permanent per event.

trigger:gives-gift.example: 'Whenever you give a gift' (Jolly Gerbils): a trigger on the gift actually being given — as an instant or sorcery with a promised gift resolves, or as a permanent's gift trigger resolves — not on the promise at cast.

trigger:sacrifice-batch-trigger.example: A batched "whenever you sacrifice one or more [filter]" trigger, firing once per simultaneous sacrifice event rather than once per permanent (Camellia, the Seedmiser's Foods).

effect:cast-now-pay-life-for-mana-value.example: cast-now with an alternative cost of life equal to the spell's mana value rather than its mana cost (Bismuth Mindrender).

effect:energy-count-amount.example: An EffectAmount for the energy counters a player has ('where X is the amount of {E} you have' - Razorfield Ripper).

cost:cost-reduction-energy-paid-this-tur.example: A per-turn stat of energy paid or lost, and a spell cost reduction per unit of it (Blaster Hulk).

cost:returned-for-cost-lki.example: The permanent returned to hand by a returnToHand cost, readable by the effect as it last existed (its subtypes - Wonderscape Sage's 'unless that land had a nonbasic land type').

decision:choose-land-type-on-resolution.example: Choose a (nonbasic) land type as a spell resolves, with a filter reading the chosen land type (March from Velis Vel).

effect:copy-spell-retarget-another-oppon.example: A cast trigger gated on another opponent controlling a permanent the spell could target, then a copy targeting one such permanent the controller chooses (Exterminator Magmarch).

bug:delayed-trigger-carries-lost-trigger.example: createDelayedTrigger carries the creating ability's trigger object at its current zoneChangeCount without checking refs.triggerObjectAfterLeaving, so a card that changed zones again before the creating trigger resolved is still followed (Desert Warfare; Avacyn, Angel of Horror and other dies -> delayed-return cards likely share it).

keyword:two-kicker-costs.example: Two different kicker costs on one card ('Kicker {G} and/or {1}{U}', rule 702.33d), each payable once, with conditions that name which kicker was paid (Wastescape Battlemage, the Zendikar Rising-style 'kicked with its {X} kicker' cards).

replacement:as-enters-choose-characteris.example: 'As this enters, it becomes your choice of [P/T and keyword sets]' — a choice made as it enters that sets copiable values (layer 1), so copies keep it (Corrupted Shapeshifter, Primal Clay).

effect:search-to-linked-exile-face-down.example: Search a library and exile the found card face down, linked to the source (rule 607.2), for later abilities to turn face up and put onto the battlefield or into a hand (The Creation of Avacyn's chapters).

cost:exile-from-graveyard-card-types.example: A cost (escape's, here) exiling any number of cards from your graveyard chosen so they have N or more card types among them, rather than a fixed count — Nethergoyf.

stat:granted-once-per-turn-per-grantor.example: 'This ability triggers only once each turn' on a statically granted triggered ability, tracked per grant instance (per granting object, rule 400.7) instead of by the ability's index in the recipient's trigger list — Cursed Wombat's rulings on two Wombats and a Wombat replaced the same turn.

effect:aggregate-all-counters.example: A sum of every counter of every kind on permanents matching a filter — 'X is the number of counters on permanents you control' (Hydra Trainer); AggregateOf counts one named kind. The no-target sibling of effect:aggregate-all-counters-for-target.

effect:grant-ability-to-permanent-spell.example: An effect (a cast trigger's resolution) that grants an ability to a permanent spell on the stack which carries to the permanent it becomes (rule 400.7a) — Thief of Existence's 'If you do, Thief of Existence gains "When this creature leaves the battlefield, target opponent draws a card."'

cost:cost-reduction-count-other.example: A cost reduction counting "each OTHER [permanent] you control" (CostReductionAmount countOf with excludeSelf) — Etherium Pteramander's "{1} less to activate for each other artifact you control".

condition:additional-cost-option-paid.example: A condition reading which additionalCost.options branch was paid — Lethal Throwdown's "sacrifice a creature or sacrifice a modified creature … If the modified creature was sacrificed, draw a card".

effect:owner-chooses-library-position.example: A permanent's owner chooses where in their library it goes — Deem Inferior's "second from the top or on the bottom".

mechanic:exalted-counters.example: Exalted counters (rule 122.1b): each gives the permanent an instance of exalted — needs exalted as a keyword whose instances the attacks-alone pump counts (Emissary of Soulfire).

replacement:enters-with-keyword.example: An enters-battlefield replacement that has the permanent enter with a keyword (haste) as an effect timestamped as it enters, optionally gated on how it was cast (kicked) — Voidpouncer's "if this creature was kicked, it enters with ... and with haste".

replacement:counter-replacement-you-put.example: A would-add-counter replacement that applies only when its controller is the player putting the counters ('If you would put one or more counters on a permanent you control' — Doc Samson; 122.6a for entering counters): counterTotal would need the putting player (addCounter's `by`).

static:your-life-total-cant-change.example: "Your life total can't change" as a static on a permanent (Platinum Emperion), not the temporary player-effect Teferi's Protection uses.

static:player-protection-from-opponents.example: "You have protection from each of your opponents" (Absolute Virtue, rule 702.16k): a static player protection from anything opponents control.

replacement:player-counter-addend.example: "If you would get one or more counters, you get that many plus one" (Winding Constrictor): the counter-addend replacement over a player's counters.

effect:grant-instant-speed-loyalty-until.example: "Until end of turn, you may activate loyalty abilities of [filter] planeswalkers you control … any time you could cast an instant" (Jace's Machinations): instant-speed loyalty granted for a duration.

effect:exile-spell-as-it-resolves-linked.example: An optional "you may exile that spell instead of putting it into its owner's graveyard as it resolves", the card exiled linked to the source (rule 607.2a) so a later "cards exiled with this" ability reaches it (Forger's Foundry); exile-spell-as-it-resolves is mandatory and unlinked.

trigger:activates-ability-targeting.example: An activates-ability trigger narrowed to abilities with a target of a given kind (Ertha Jo: "whenever you activate an ability that targets a creature or player").

trigger:damage-equal-to-toughness.example: A deals-damage trigger clause matching only damage to a creature equal to that creature's toughness (ignoring damage already marked) — Taii Wakeen.

replacement:damage-plus-x-this-turn.example: An effect (from an activated ability) creating a this-turn would-deal-damage +X replacement for sources you control, X fixed at resolution — Taii Wakeen's {X},{T} ability.

effect:count-target-players-not-done-thi.example: An amount counting the players in an any-number target slot for whom a this-way result didn't happen ("for each of those opponents who didn't discard a card with mana value 4 or greater, draw a card" — Hollow Marauder), after a simultaneous for-each-target discard.

trigger:becomes-attached.example: A 'whenever an Aura [you control] becomes attached to [filter]' trigger carrying the Aura and the permanent, so an intervening comparison (mana value of the permanent <= the Aura's) and the effect can read both (Eriette, the Beguiler).

effect:control-while-attached.example: gain-control 'for as long as that Aura is attached to it': the control effect ends when a named Aura leaves or becomes unattached from the permanent, and does nothing if it already has as the ability resolves (Eriette, the Beguiler's ruling).

decision:choose-face-up-exiled-card.example: Choose (without targeting) a face-up card in exile that a given player owns as an effect resolves, and move it to another zone — Binding Negotiation's 'you may put a face-up exiled card they own into their graveyard'.

condition:controlled-as-cast.example: 'If you controlled a [filter] as you cast this spell' — a board condition snapshotted when the spell finished being cast and read on resolution, not asked again then (Steer Clear).

effect:temporary-counter-addend.example: A player-effect 'until end of turn, if you would put one or more +1/+1 counters on a creature you control, put that many plus one instead', cumulative per resolution and reaching enters-with-counters (Prairie Dog).

bug:cda-turn-stat.example: A CDA count (setBasePtFromCount's CountSpec) that reads a per-player turn stat, e.g. cards drawn this turn — Duelist of the Mind's '*/3, power equal to the number of cards you've drawn this turn'.

effect:look-and-choose-unlinked-exile.example: A look-and-choose exile that isn't a linked ability: destination 'exile' always records exiledWith on the source's stint (rule 607.2a), so a later copied 'the exiled card' ability on the same permanent finds it (Lazav, Familiar Stranger's 'you may exile a card from a graveyard', then becoming a copy of it).

effect:token-copy-each-other.example: create-token-copy's { each } filter leaving out the effect's source — 'for each other nonland permanent you control, create a token that's a copy of that permanent' (Oko, the Ringleader's −5).

cost:plot-cost-reduction.example: A static that changes the cost of the plot special action (rule 702.170a) — Doc Aurlock's "Plotting cards from your hand costs {2} less" (generic only).

static:pt-per-cards-in-hand.example: grantPtPerCount counting the cards in a player's hand — Stingerback Terror's "gets -1/-1 for each card in your hand" (layer 7c, not a base P/T characteristic-defining ability).

effect:reflexive-refers-to-parent-target.example: A reflexive ('When you do, …') trigger's effect acting on the creating ability's own target without targeting it again — Behemoth of Vault 0's 'you may pay {E} equal to target nonland permanent's mana value. When you do, destroy that permanent.'

effect:reflexive-per-counters-placed.example: A reflexive trigger that fires once per N counters actually placed by the step before it (Craig Boone's 'put two quest counters … When you do' — twice under Doubling Season, per its ruling).

effect:restrict-rule-for-player.example: A turn-wide restrict rule (rule 611.2c, binding later arrivals) over creatures one chosen player controls — 'creatures that player controls without flying can't block this turn' (The Motherlode, Excavator), the defending player or a target's controller.

effect:target-creature-blocking-attached.example: A target spec / filter clause for a creature blocking the Equipment's (or Aura's) host — Plasma Caster's 'target creature that's blocking equipped creature'.

static:doesnt-untap-attached.example: 'Equipped creature doesn't untap during its controller's untap step' — doesntUntap on an attached (or filtered) scope rather than the static's own permanent (T-45 Power Armor).

trigger:discards-first-time-each-turn.example: A firstTimeEachTurn on the discards trigger, read off the turn's discards before the source arrived too — 'whenever you discard one or more nonland cards for the first time each turn' (Veronica, Dissident Scribe).

zone:play-exiled-this-way-after-choice.example: Granting a play permission (lands included) this turn to the card an earlier step of the same resolution exiled, after a choice in between — Synth Eradicator's 'exile the top card … You may get {E}{E}. If you don't, you may play that card this turn.'

effect:base-power-amount.example: An EffectAmount reading an object's base power (after layer 7b, last-known if gone) — Curie, Emergent Intelligence's 'draw cards equal to its base power'.

effect:target-per-graveyard-with-match.example: 'For each graveyard with an [X] card in it, exile target [X] card from that graveyard' — one mandatory target slot per graveyard that has a match, none for one that doesn't (Mysterious Stranger).

static:activated-abilities-of-exiled-wit.example: Rex, Cyber-Hound: 'has all activated abilities of all cards in exile with brain counters on them' — like grantsActivatedOfLinkedExile, but over every exiled card carrying a counter kind, not just cards linked to this permanent.

cost:cost-reduction-creatures-attacking-.example: Sentry Bot: 'costs {1} less to cast for each creature attacking you' — a CostReductionAmount counting creatures attacking the caster (the { attackingPlayer } EffectAmount's count).

static:graveyard-cast-filter-amount.example: Arcade Gannon: a castFromGraveyard permission whose filter compares against an amount ('mana value less than or equal to the number of quest counters on Arcade Gannon') — the permission's filter is matched without FilterContext.amount, so it fails closed.

effect:random-permanent.example: The Nipton Lottery: 'choose a creature at random' on the battlefield, untargeted, then act on it (and on all others) — choose-random-card reads only a graveyard.

effect:reveal-cards-from-hand.example: Vault 21: House Gambit: 'reveal up to five nonland cards from your hand' as an effect, then a count over the revealed set (cards sharing a mana value with another revealed card).

effect:attach-to-chosen-creature.example: Vault 101: Birthday Party: 'you may attach it to a creature you control' — attach an Equipment just put onto the battlefield to a creature chosen as the effect resolves, without targeting (AUTHORING §6 attach: 'Not yet … to a creature chosen without targeting').

keyword:scavenge.example: Scavenge (rule 702.97): exile the card from your graveyard and pay its scavenge cost to put +1/+1 counters equal to its power on target creature, sorcery speed — printed, and granted to graveyard cards with the cost equal to their mana cost (Young Deathclaws).

cost:cost-reduction-all-counters.example: Lumbering Megasloth: 'costs {1} less to cast for each counter among players and permanents' — a CostReductionAmount summing every counter of every kind on every permanent and player.

effect:aura-token-copies-attached.example: Three Dog, Galaxy News DJ: an optional cost of sacrificing an Aura attached to the source, and a reflexive 'for each other attacking creature you control, create a token copy of that Aura attached to that creature' (untargeted, skipped where it couldn't legally attach).

mechanic:secret-choice.example: Players choose secretly and reveal simultaneously: a secret vote (for objects or named options) and 'each secretly choose a number' (Vault 11: Voter's Dilemma, Expert-Level Safe).

keyword:enlist.example: Enlist (rule 702.154): as it attacks, optionally tap a nonattacking, non-sick creature you control to add its power until end of turn; plus an 'if it enlisted a creature this combat' condition (Aradesh, the Founder).

keyword:fortify.example: Fortification artifacts and Fortify [cost] (rule 702.67): attach to a land you control at sorcery speed, with a 'fortified land' scope and triggers (C.A.M.P.).

static:pt-per-counters-among-permanents.example: grantPtPerCount by the number of counters of one kind among permanents a player controls ('+1/+1 for each quest counter among permanents you control' — Moira Brown's Wasteland Survival Guide).

effect:grant-escape-until-end-of-turn.example: A one-shot 'target card in your graveyard gains escape until end of turn', escape cost its mana cost plus exiling N other graveyard cards (Desdemona, Freedom's Edge).

effect:restrict-all-target-player.example: A combat restriction over every creature a target player controls ('creatures target player controls can't block this turn' — Headliner Scarlett): restrict's filter can't point at a target player.

condition:attacking-player-left-an-oppon.example: Intervening-if on a 'player attacks you' trigger: the attacking player has another opponent who isn't being attacked (Suppressor Skyguard).

trigger:mentors.example: Aegis of the Legion: 'Whenever equipped creature mentors a creature' — a trigger on a mentor ability of the attached (or own) creature resolving and putting its counter, with the mentored creature as the trigger object.

effect:sacrifice-all-but-up-to-n.example: Covetous Elegy: 'each player chooses up to N creatures they control, then sacrifices the rest' with fewer allowed (min 0), each player asked in APNAP order knowing earlier choices, every unchosen permanent sacrificed at once — sacrifice-all-but keeps exactly N and sacrifices player by player.

keyword:collect-evidence.example: Collect evidence N (rule 701.59): exile any number of cards from your graveyard with total mana value N or more, possible only if the graveyard can reach N — as an additional cost, an optional 'you may collect evidence N' in an effect, and the reflexive 'when you do' after it (Memory Vampire).

static:unblockable-defending-player-cond.example: Can't be blocked as long as the defending player meets a player condition (has a rad counter — Nightkin Ambusher), checked as blocks are declared; landwalk is the only defender-condition evasion today.

effect:delayed-cast-trigger-through-play.example: A delayed trigger installed on a named player (the defending player) that fires each time they cast a spell, lasting until the end of that player's next turn (Nuka-Nuke Launcher).

effect:return-as-aura-with-granted-abili.example: Return a card to the battlefield as an Aura enchantment with a given enchant restriction (Forest you control), choosing what it enchants as it enters, granting the enchanted permanent an ability and losing all its other abilities (Harold and Bob, First Numens).

keyword:squad-nonmana-cost.example: A squad cost that isn't only mana — exiling cards from your graveyard (Ruthless Radrat) or {1} plus a discard (Thrill-Kill Disciple) — paid any number of times as the spell is cast.

replacement:life-loss-from-radiation.example: Life lost from the rad-counter trigger (rule 728.1a) marked as 'from radiation' so a replacement can change it — Strong, the Brutish Thespian's 'You gain life rather than lose life from radiation'.

stat:milled-this-turn-mill-only.example: A per-card 'milled this turn' marker set only by a mill (rule 701.17), not by surveil or other library-to-graveyard moves — Tato Farmer and The Master, Transcendent's 'card in a graveyard that was milled this turn' (their rulings exclude cards put there without the word mill).

replacement:enter-tapped-optional-rider.example: 'You may have this permanent enter tapped. If you do, [effect]' — an optional enter-tapped choice asked as it enters (rule 614.12), with an effect when taken — Mariposa Military Base's 'If you do, you get two rad counters'.

effect:goad-while-counter.example: A one-shot effect that makes a creature goaded, unable to attack you or permanents you control, and unable to block creatures you control for as long as it has a counter of a kind (Immortal Obligation's duty counter).

static:pt-per-turn-stat.example: A static P/T bonus counting a turn stat — 'creatures you control get +X/+X, where X is the number of cards you've drawn this turn' (Knowledge Is Power): grantPtPerCount with a turnStat.

effect:create-token-enters-with-counters.example: A created token that enters with N counters (a replacement as it enters, rule 614.1c), not thenCounters' put-after: 'The token enters with X +1/+1 counters on it' (Printlifter Ooze).

static:trigger-doubler-turned-face-up.example: A doubleTriggers cause for a face-down permanent turning face up (Panoptic Projektor).

effect:choose-new-targets-any-number.example: 'You may choose new targets for any number of other spells and/or abilities' (Boltbender): an untargeted change-targets over a chosen set of stack objects.

effect:exile-self-with-time-counters.example: A resolving spell exiles itself with N time counters, becoming suspended again if it has suspend (Charnel Serenade).

zone:play-from-graveyard-surveilled-this.example: Play lands and cast spells from among graveyard cards you put there by surveilling this turn, paying life equal to mana value instead of the mana cost (Eye of Duskmantle).

keyword:unleash.example: Unleash (rule 702.98): may enter with a +1/+1 counter; can't block while it has one — printed, and granted to entering creatures by a static (Tesak, Judith's Hellhound).

effect:copy-spell-for-each-chosen-paid.example: Copy a spell once for each of any number of chosen objects it could target, paying a cost per copy, each copy targeting its object (Feather, Radiant Arbiter).

stat:permanents-to-graveyard-from-battle.example: A turn count of permanents put into graveyards from the battlefield (any controller, tokens included, filterable by type) — gravestorm, Anzrag's Rampage's artifacts.

effect:ungoad.example: 'Each creature you control is no longer goaded' (Serene Sleuth): end every goad on matching creatures.

effect:exile-top-face-down-linked.example: Exile the top card of a library face down where nobody may look at it ('You can't look at it'), linked to the source (rule 607.2a) with no play permission — Connecting the Dots.

condition:put-into-graveyard-this-turn-f.example: A CardFilter clause for a card in a graveyard that was put there from anywhere this turn (not only from a library) — Reenact the Crime.

effect:look-and-choose-cloak.example: A look-and-choose destination that cloaks the chosen cards (face-down 2/2s with ward {2}, rule 701.58) rather than manifesting them — Hide in Plain Sight.

effect:amount-color-pairs.example: An amount counting the different color pairs among permanents matching a filter that are exactly two colors — Niv-Mizzet, Guildpact.

keyword:hexproof-from-multicolored.example: Hexproof from multicolored (rule 702.11d): can't be the target of multicolored spells or abilities from multicolored sources opponents control — Niv-Mizzet, Guildpact.

condition:filter-dealt-damage-this-turn.example: A CardFilter clause for a permanent that dealt damage this turn to anything (players, planeswalkers, creatures) — Treacherous Greed's sacrifice cost.

effect:choose-per-player-untargeted.example: For each player, the controller chooses up to one permanent that player controls (untargeted), the chosen ones are acted on together, then each affected permanent's controller may follow up — Krenko's Buzzcrusher.

bug:cda-count-multiplier.example: A setBasePtFromCount multiplier for a CDA of 'twice the number of …' — Melek, Reforged Researcher.

condition:player-controls-most.example: A player scope or that-player condition for 'each player who controls the most [filter]' (ties included) — No Witnesses.

cost:disguise-x-cost.example: A morph/disguise cost with {X} (Aurelia's Vindicator's Disguise {X}{3}{W}): the turn-face-up special action announces X, and its turned-face-up trigger reads it ("up to X targets").

effect:cast-now-from-each-opponent-grave.example: "You may cast a spell from each opponent's graveyard without paying its mana cost" (Jetsam): an untargeted cast-now offered once per opponent from that player's graveyard, chosen as the effect resolves (after an earlier step such as a mill).

static:cant-become-suspected.example: A static that stops affected creatures from becoming suspected (Airtight Alibi's "enchanted creature ... can't become suspected"), checked by Game.suspect.

effect:put-onto-battlefield-attached.example: Put an Aura/Equipment card onto the battlefield attached to a named permanent (Magnetic Snuffler's "return target Equipment card from your graveyard to the battlefield attached to this creature"), entering unattached when it can't legally attach.

cost:disguise-cost-reduction.example: A disguise (or morph) cost reduced by a live count as it's paid — Fugitive Codebreaker's "Disguise {5}{R}. This cost is reduced by {1} for each instant and sorcery card in your graveyard".

static:cant-turn-face-up.example: A static that stops a set of permanents being turned face up, by any cost — Karlov Watchdog's "Permanents your opponents control can't be turned face up during your turn".

effect:look-and-choose-revealed-card-des.example: One revealed card whose destination depends on it and the chooser — Break Out's "you may reveal a creature card … If that card has mana value 2 or less, you may put it onto the battlefield … If you didn't, put it into your hand" (a second pick that keeps the first's reveal:"chosen").

replacement:as-turned-face-up-dynamic-co.example: `asTurnedFaceUp` counters as an amount read as it's turned face up — Crowd-Control Warden's "put X +1/+1 counters on it, where X is the number of other creatures you control".

decision:secret-choice.example: A choice made secretly on resolution (hidden from other players, remembered per permanent) and a "reveal the [choice]" activation cost only the chooser can pay — A Killer Among Us.

stat:sacrificed-this-turn.example: Turn tally of the permanents a player sacrificed, by type — Suspicious Detonation's "if you've sacrificed an artifact this turn" as a selfCostReduction condition.

trigger:dealt-damage-amount-threshold.example: A `dealt-damage` trigger gated on the amount of one damage event — Innocent Bystander's "Whenever this creature is dealt 3 or more damage" (all at once, not cumulative).

effect:must-block-this-turn.example: A 'blocks this turn if able' requirement on a target creature (rule 509.1c) — Hustle's 'attacks or blocks this turn if able'; the `restrict` effect has must-attack but no must-block.

effect:look-at-face-down-permanents.example: 'Until end of turn, you may look at face-down creatures you don't control any time' (Lumbering Laundry): a per-player view permission over other players' face-down permanents (not spells), lasting until end of turn.

keyword:collect-evidence-x.example: Collect evidence X with a variable X: chosen as an effect resolves and read by what follows ('you may collect evidence X. When you do, ... X damage' — Incinerator of the Guilty), or computed as a mandatory additional cost from the spell's targets' total mana value (Urgent Necropsy).

decision:ward-collect-evidence.example: 'Ward—Collect evidence N' (Axebane Ferox): the targeting player may exile cards from their graveyard with total mana value N or more, payable only if their graveyard holds that much; otherwise the spell or ability is countered.

effect:extract-same-name.example: Exile a chosen card from an opponent's graveyard, then search its owner's graveyard, hand and library for any number of cards with that name and exile them; that player shuffles (Deadly Cover-Up then has them draw a card for each card exiled from their hand).

cost:alt-cost-collect-evidence-for-spell.example: 'You may collect evidence N rather than pay the mana cost for spells you cast' (Conspiracy Unraveler): a static alternative cost for every spell that is a collect-evidence payment, not mana; it isn't the spell's own 'if evidence was collected' and can't use the card being cast from the graveyard.

effect:may-exile-self-and-collect-eviden.example: 'You may exile it and collect evidence N. If you do, ...' (Lamplight Phoenix) as one optional action: offered only if the dies-trigger's card is still in the graveyard and the rest of the graveyard (not that card) holds N mana value, the collect then mandatory, 'if you do' only when both happened.

cost:collect-evidence-linked-exile.example: Cards exiled by an activated ability's collect-evidence cost linked to its source (rule 607.2a) so a later ability can read 'cards exiled with it' (Kylox's Voltstrider).

effect:cast-now-bottom-of-library-after.example: cast-now's 'if that spell would be put into a graveyard, put it on the bottom of its owner's library instead' — exileAfter's twin for the library bottom (Kylox's Voltstrider).

condition:distinct-damage-sources-this-t.example: 'N or more sources you controlled dealt damage this turn' — distinct sources, each object-and-stint once however often it dealt damage (Case of the Burning Masks).

cost:cost-reduction-if-kicked.example: 'This spell costs {N} less to cast if [its optional additional cost was paid]' — a reduction on the kicked variant only (Bite Down on Crime: if evidence was collected).

static:may-choose-not-to-untap.example: 'You may choose not to untap this creature during your untap step' — an untap-step choice for its controller (Hedge Whisperer).

effect:duration-while-source-tapped.example: A modifier lasting 'for as long as [this source] remains tapped', ending when it untaps or leaves (Hedge Whisperer).

effect:grant-graveyard-cast-all.example: The mass form of grant-graveyard-cast: each card in your graveyard matching a filter as it resolves gains 'you may cast this card from your graveyard' until end of turn, the set fixed at resolution (rule 611.2c — Case of the Uneaten Feast).

static:look-at-top-card-conditional.example: 'You may look at the top card of your library any time' gated on a condition (a Case's solved designation, a Class level) — looksAtOwnLibraryTop is an unconditional card-level flag (Case of the Locked Hothouse).

effect:surveil-kept-on-top-count.example: An EffectAmount for the number of cards a surveil (or scry) just kept on top of the library — Starving Revenant's 'for each card you put on top of your library, you draw a card and you lose 3 life' (looked minus movedAway of the scried event).

cost:exile-permanents-total-mana-value-x.example: An activation cost exiling one or more other permanents you control matching a filter, whose total mana value is the ability's X — Fabrication Foundry's 'Exile one or more other artifacts you control with total mana value X: return target artifact card with mana value X or less'.

effect:target-player-exiles-from-hand.example: A targeted player exiles a card of their choice from their own hand (Skullcap Snail: "target opponent exiles a card from their hand") — a choose-from-zone over the target player's hand, asked of them, the card exiled unlinked.

replacement:turn-exile-if-dies-filter.example: A resolving spell installs a would-die exile-instead replacement over a filter for the rest of the turn, read live so creatures that enter or change control later are covered (Malicious Eclipse: "If a creature an opponent controls would die this turn, exile it instead").

cost:cost-reduction-sum.example: A spell's cost reduction that adds two counts — permanents on the battlefield plus cards in a graveyard ('{1} less for each Cave you control and each Cave card in your graveyard' — Gargantuan Leech); CostReductionAmount has no sum.

static:look-at-top-card-granted.example: Grant "you may look at the top card of your library any time" to another permanent (Glowcap Lantern's equipped creature): looksAtOwnLibraryTop is read only off a permanent's own definition.

effect:opponents-controlling-count.example: An EffectAmount: the number of opponents (or players) who control a permanent matching a filter — Journey On's "one plus the number of opponents who control an artifact".

effect:explore-each.example: "Each [creature] explores" (rule 701.44d): every matching permanent explores in one resolution, the controller choosing the order (APNAP across controllers) — Hakbal of the Surging Soul.

replacement:explore-replacement.example: Replace an exploration: "if a creature you control would explore, instead …" — scry 1 first (Twists and Turns), explore twice (Topography Tracker); each copy applies once more (the rulings).

stat:cast-using-mana-from-this-source.example: A cast trigger on a permanent keyed to mana that permanent itself produced ('whenever you cast a permanent spell using mana produced by Tecutlan'): record the producing object on each ManaUnit and let a cast-spell trigger filter on 'mana from this source was spent', firing once per spell and only while the source is on the battlefield.

effect:discover-by-other-player.example: Discover performed by a player other than the effect's controller ('that player discovers X' — Zoyowa's Justice): exile from that player's library, their free-cast-or-hand choice, their discovers triggers.

static:keywords-from-exiled-with-source.example: A permanent has a keyword as long as a card exiled with it (one used to craft it, rule 702.167c) has that keyword — Wretched Bonemass's flying, first strike, … protection, reach, trample and vigilance.

effect:prohibit-abilities-while-tapped.example: "Tap target permanent. Its activated abilities can't be activated for as long as it remains tapped" (Braided Net): a prohibit on one permanent that ends when it untaps (or leaves), not at end of turn.

replacement:as-enters-choose-card-type-o.example: As a crafted permanent enters, choose a card type shared among the exiled cards used to craft it, readable by its other abilities (Apex Observatory).

effect:next-spell-of-type-free-this-turn.example: "The next spell you cast this turn of the chosen type can be cast without paying its mana cost" (Apex Observatory): a one-use free-cast permission for the controller, lasting this turn.

effect:attached-becomes-copy-of-chosen-e.example: As an Equipment becomes attached, choose an exiled creature card used to craft it; the equipped creature is a copy of the last chosen card (Dinosaur Headdress).

condition:filter-double-faced.example: A CardFilter clause for double-faced cards and permanents — Tetzin, Gnome Champion's "another double-faced artifact you control enters", The Golden-Gear Colossus's "target double-faced artifact you control".

effect:choose-per-player-destroy-rest.example: For each player, the effect's controller chooses a creature matching a filter that player controls, then destroys all creatures except those chosen (Unstable Glyphbridge; must choose one if able, the ruling).

effect:player-cant-attack-you-this-turn.example: "They can't attack you or planeswalkers you control this turn" (Sandswirl Wanderglyph, on an opponent casting a spell during their turn): a player-level attack prohibition for the rest of the turn, lasting though the source leaves.

static:attacked-you-cant-cast-spells.example: "Each opponent who attacked you or a planeswalker you control this turn can't cast spells" (Sandswirl Wanderglyph): a static prohibition on players who attacked its controller this turn.

trigger:exiled-while-crafting.example: "When this creature is exiled from the battlefield while you're activating a craft ability" (Market Gnome): a leaves-battlefield-to-exile trigger limited to exiles made while its controller activates a craft ability (as a material, or by a mana ability paying for it).

bug:granted-flashback-split-card-cost.example: Return the Past: Granted flashback 'equal to its mana cost' uses the split card's combined cost instead of the cast half's (rule 702.34 rulings; Return the Past, also Iroh, Grand Lotus / Lier / Will of the Jeskai).

condition:that-player-turn-stat.example: Davros, Dalek Creator: turn-stat read for the 'that-player' of a for-each-player / each-player-may - 'each opponent who lost 3 or more life this turn' (Davros); sibling of condition:target-player-turn-stat.

cost:escape-exile-permanent.example: Lunar Hatchling: An escape cost that exiles a permanent you control (Lunar Hatchling).

cost:exile-permanents-may.example: Fugitive of the Judoon: 'You may exile a [X] you control and a [Y] you control. If you do, …' — two distinct permanents, offered only when both exist (Fugitive of the Judoon).

cost:exiled-card-ref.example: Jhoira of the Ghitu: "Exile a nonland card from your hand" as a cost, then "put four time counters on the exiled card": the effect has no reference to the card the cost exiled.

decision:choose-permanents-non-target.example: The Day of the Doctor: 'Choose up to three Doctors' then act on all others (The Day of the Doctor IV) — choose-permanents exists, but the 'all other creatures' exile needs to read the chosen set.

decision:opponent-guesses-mana-value.example: The Seventh Doctor: An opponent guesses about a face-down chosen card (The Seventh Doctor).

effect:amount-total-power-died-this-turn.example: Genesis of the Daleks: Sum of the power (as last on the battlefield) of creatures matching a filter that died this turn - Genesis of the Daleks IV.

effect:become-copy-while-target-tapped.example: Zygon Infiltrator: become a copy for as long as another permanent remains tapped (Zygon Infiltrator)

effect:cast-paying-suspend-cost.example: The Face of Boe: Cast a card from hand paying its suspend cost as an alternative cost (The Face of Boe).

effect:choose-opponent-most-life.example: The Master, Gallifrey's End: choose-opponent limited to the opponents with the most life (ties: you choose) - The Master, Gallifrey's End.

effect:create-token-attached-to.example: The Rani: create-token entering attached to a target permanent (an Aura token with enchant creature) - The Rani's Mark of the Rani.

effect:exile-becomes-foretold.example: The Foretold Soldier: Exile a permanent face down as foretold (The Foretold Soldier).

effect:exile-to-library-bottom-linked.example: Trial of a Time Lord: Put every card exiled with this source (an O-Ring's exiles) on the bottom of its owner's library (Trial of a Time Lord IV).

effect:goad-extensions.example: The War Games: I: tokens 'goaded for as long as this Saga remains on the battlefield'; only goad-until-your-next-turn and goadedForGame exist.

effect:goad-while-controlled-by-player.example: Vislor Turlough: A one-shot goad by the effect's controller lasting for as long as a named player controls the creature (Vislor Turlough).

effect:per-target-villainous-choice-turn.example: Hunted by The Family: For each of several targets, its controller faces a villainous choice, asked in turn order (the ruling) - Hunted by The Family.

effect:phase-out-while-source-tapped.example: The Pandorica: phased out until the source untaps or leaves (The Pandorica)

effect:phased-out-this-way-count.example: Out of Time: Vanishing is built; "a time counter for each creature that phased out this way" has no this-way count of phasing.

effect:player-shuffles-chosen-permanent-.example: This Is How It Ends: A player (the target's owner) chooses a permanent they own and shuffles it into their library; also needs an owner-of-target scope - This Is How It Ends.

effect:put-into-combat-attacking.example: Midnight Crusader Shuttle: Make a permanent already on the battlefield an attacking creature attacking a given player (not declared, so no attack triggers) - Midnight Crusader Shuttle.

effect:remove-time-counters-chosen-suspe.example: Amy Pond: "Choose a suspended card you own and remove that many time counters from it": a choice among suspended cards in exile, then a removal there.

effect:search-up-to-public-zone.example: The Five Doctors: A search for 'up to N' cards including a graveyard must allow finding zero there; the engine forces ≥1 whenever a graveyard match exists (The Five Doctors).

effect:stops-being-creature.example: Blink: 'This permanent isn't a creature until end of turn' — remove the creature type (and creature subtypes) for a duration (Blink's Alien Angel token).

effect:stops-being-creature-until-eot.example: Weeping Angel: 'This creature isn't a creature until end of turn' - removes the creature type and creature subtypes, keeping the other types (Weeping Angel's ruling).

filter:has-doctors-companion.example: An Unearthly Child: Match a card with the doctor's companion pairing ability (An Unearthly Child).

filter:shares-creature-type-with-target.example: Coward // Killer: Coward's time travel is built; Killer's "each other creature that shares a creature type with it" needs sharesCreatureTypeWith keyed to a target slot (it reads only a trigger object).

keyword:fuse.example: Gallifrey Falls // No More: fuse (rule 702.102): cast both halves from hand

mechanic:commander-chosen-color-pregame.example: Clara Oswald: If this is your commander, choose a color before the game; it is that color (and its color identity follows) — Clara Oswald.

replacement:combat-damage-to-creature-pr.example: Weeping Angel: If this would deal combat damage to a creature, prevent it and that creature's owner shuffles it into their library - Weeping Angel.

replacement:draw-from-bottom.example: River Song: A static that makes its controller draw from the bottom of their library (River Song).

replacement:enter-as-copy-of-exiled-card.example: The Master, Formed Anew: Enter as a copy of a creature card in exile matching a filter (a takeover counter on it) - The Master, Formed Anew.

replacement:enter-from-exile-shuffle-ins.example: Don't Blink: Turn-long replacement on creatures entering from exile or cast from exile (Don't Blink).

replacement:villainous-choice-additional.example: The Valeyard: If an opponent would face a villainous choice, they face it an additional time - The Valeyard.

static:counters-remain-across-zones.example: Me, the Immortal: Counters stay on the card as it changes zones (Me, the Immortal).

static:extra-vote.example: The Valeyard: 'While voting, you may vote an additional time' (rule 701.38d) - The Valeyard.

static:gains-abilities-of-exiled-card.example: Idris, Soul of the TARDIS: Vanishing is built; "Idris has all activated and triggered abilities of the exiled card and gets +X/+X" isn't.

static:must-be-blocked-by-filter.example: Ace's Baseball Bat: 'must be blocked by a [Dalek] if able' - only one matching creature is required to block (Ace's Baseball Bat rulings).

static:play-from-library-top-once-each-t.example: The Fourth Doctor: A once-each-turn play/cast from the library top, with a 'when you do' rider (The Fourth Doctor).

static:unblockable-unless-attacking-owne.example: Become the Pilot: can't be blocked unless attacking its owner or a permanent its owner controls (Become the Pilot)

target:controlled-by-chosen-player.example: Strax, Sontaran Nurse: A reflexive trigger's target filtered to the player the creating effect chose (random or not) — Strax's 'another target creature that player controls'.

trigger:activates-ability-targets-only-s.example: Bill Potts: An activated-ability trigger filtered on the ability's targets (only this permanent), sharing a once-each-turn limit with a spell trigger (Bill Potts).

trigger:attacks-and-isnt-blocked.example: Cybermat: Per-creature 'whenever this creature attacks and isn't blocked', firing as blockers are declared - Cybermat.

trigger:cast-spell-with-cascade.example: The First Doctor: cast-spell trigger filter: the spell has cascade (printed or granted)

trigger:combat-damage-to-owner.example: The Beast, Deathless Prince: a creature deals combat damage to its owner (The Beast)

trigger:functions-while-suspended.example: Deep-Sea Kraken: "Whenever an opponent casts a spell, if this card is suspended, remove a time counter from it": a trigger working from exile.

trigger:phases-out.example: The War Doctor: "whenever one or more other permanents phase out" (rule 603.10b)

bug:look-and-choose-offers-unattachable-.example: Knickknack Ouphe: look-and-choose with destination battlefield offers Auras with nothing they could enchant (rule 303.4g); a chosen one stays where it is in the library and misses the leftover move (bottom/graveyard). condition:source-enchanted-by-n-auras.example: Timber Paladin: StaticCondition: the source is enchanted by exactly N (or at least N) Auras — Timber Paladin

cost:sacrifice-attached-aura.example: Faunsbane Troll: "Sacrifice an Aura attached to this creature" as a cost, and "if that creature would die this turn, exile it instead".

effect:create-token-attached-each.example: Asinine Antics: "For each creature your opponents control, create a Cursed Role token attached to that creature": one token per matching permanent, each attached to its own — `attachedTo` names one permanent. (Also its "flash if you pay {2} more".)

effect:delayed-trigger-next-combat-phase.example: Feral Encounter: Delayed trigger timing "at the beginning of the next combat phase this turn" (Feral Encounter); none if no combat follows.

filter:has-adventure.example: Sentinel of Lost Lore: CardFilter clause for a card/spell/permanent that has an Adventure (an adventurer card's alternative characteristics), not matching an instant/sorcery cast as an Adventure on the stack (the WOE rulings)

mechanic:celebration.example: Wilds of Eldraine: Celebration's 'two or more nonland permanents entered the battlefield under your control this turn' — now built as CELEBRATION_CONDITION over the existing entered turn history; add the key to the gaps file's built array.

trigger:you-tap-opponents-creature.example: Icewrought Sentry: Icewrought Sentry: 'whenever you tap an untapped creature an opponent controls' — a becomes-tapped trigger narrowed to a tap caused by an effect/cost the trigger's controller controls, of an opponent's previously untapped creature.

zone:cast-from-library-top-once-each-tur.example: Johann, Apprentice Sorcerer: castFromLibraryTop with a once-per-turn allowance per permanent (Johann, Apprentice Sorcerer), like castFromGraveyard.oncePerTurn.

effect:copy-next-loyalty-ability.example: Jaya's Phoenix: "Copy the next loyalty ability you activate this turn when you activate it": a delayed copy of an activation.

effect:manifest-count-amount.example: Omarthis, Ghostfire Initiate: "Manifest a number of cards equal to the number of counters on it": `manifest`'s count is a fixed number.

effect:animate-planeswalker-with-trigger.example: Sparkshaper Visionary: Any number of planeswalkers become 3/3 Bird creatures (no longer planeswalkers) with a granted "scry 1" combat-damage trigger until end of turn.

condition:ring-bearer-other-than-source.example: Galadriel of Lothlórien, Faramir, Field Commander: "whenever the Ring tempts you, if you chose a creature other than ~ as your Ring-bearer".

effect:exile-graveyard-may-cast.example: Shadow of the Enemy: exile a graveyard, then you may cast spells from among the cards exiled this way, spending mana as any type.

trigger:played-card-exiled-this-way.example: Fires of Mount Doom: a delayed "when you play a card exiled this way" trigger tied to an impulse exile.

target:power-less-than-source.example: Rangers of Ithilien: "target creature with lesser power" than the source, on targeting and resolution.

static:monarch-controls-enchanted.example: Fealty to the Realm: the monarch controls enchanted creature, at the Aura's timestamp.

condition:revealed-shares-type-with-spel.example: Gandalf, Westward Voyager: each opponent reveals the top card; if any shares a card type with the spell.

filter:least-among-its-controller.example: Witch-king, Bringer of Ruin: "a creature with the least power among creatures they control".

decision:opponent-guesses-card-kind.example: Gollum, Scheming Guide: an opponent guesses land or nonland for your top card.

replacement:exile-if-not-cycled.example: Abandoned Sarcophagus: a card with cycling that would go to your graveyard other than by being cycled is exiled instead.

effect:counter-targeting-spell-or-abilit.example: Glyph Keeper: the first time each turn it becomes the target of a spell or ability (any player's), counter that spell or ability — only ward counters a targeting spell, always with a cost; becomes-target's firstTimeEachTurn counts per targeting player.

effect:shuffle-graveyard-filter-into-lib.example: Elixir: shuffle the nonland cards from your graveyard into your library, then gain life equal to the number shuffled — shuffle-graveyard-into-library has no filter or this-way count.

cost:crew-alternative-remove-loyalty.example: Heart of Kiran: crew by removing a loyalty counter from a planeswalker you control rather than tapping creatures.

effect:prevent-combat-damage-by-chosen-c.example: Ajani's Aid: prevent all combat damage a creature of your choice would deal this turn — chosen as it resolves, not targeted.

effect:reveal-until-per-destroyed-this-w.example: Indomitable Creativity: for each permanent destroyed this way, its controller reveals until an artifact or creature card, and all of them enter at once.

amount:creatures-dealt-combat-damage-to-.example: Excess (Indulge // Excess): 'for each creature you controlled that dealt combat damage to a player this turn' — no turn-history list records which creatures did.

cost:mana-ability-discard.example: Bog Witch: '{B}, {T}, Discard a card: Add {B}{B}{B}.' A mana ability's activation never pays `cost.discard` (only the stack path does), and activation doesn't refuse it either — docs/engine-gaps.md.

effect:discard-controller-of-target.example: Nicol Bolas, Planeswalker's −9: 'that player or that planeswalker's controller discards seven cards, then sacrifices seven permanents' — `discard` reads only a player slot.

effect:grant-embalm.example: Cursecloth Wrappings: 'target creature card in your graveyard gains embalm until end of turn. The embalm cost is equal to its mana cost.'

effect:counter-into-battlefield.example: Desertion: 'if an artifact or creature spell is countered this way, put that card onto the battlefield under your control instead of into its owner's graveyard' — `counter`'s `into` is a hand or exile.

decision:any-opponent-may.example: Sin Prodder: 'Any opponent may have you put that card into your graveyard. If a player does, …' — one opponent's yes ends it; `each-player-may` lets every opponent say yes.

replacement:clone-exception-if-embalmed.example: Vizier of Many Faces: 'except if this creature was embalmed, the token has no mana cost, it's white, and it's a Zombie' — a `copyOnEnter` exception that applies only to the embalmed token.

condition:source-monstrous.example: Colossus of Akros: 'As long as this creature is monstrous, it has trample and can attack as though it didn't have defender' — `GameObject.monstrous` is recorded but no filter or condition reads it.

condition:dice-rolled-doubles.example: Celebr-8000: roll two six-sided dice, a result table per die, and 'if you rolled doubles'.

static:equip-only-to-filter.example: O-Naginata: 'This Equipment can be attached only to a creature with power 3 or greater' — an attach restriction, and the state-based unattach when the creature stops qualifying (rule 301.5c).

mechanic:token-devour.example: Dragon Broodmother: a token with devour 2. Devour is asked only where `askEnterChoice` runs; token creation never asks, so a token's devour would never happen — docs/engine-gaps.md.
